metaDescription: Six blackout curtain sets compared on light blocking, lining, header style and fabric, so you can darken a living room or bedroom without a stiff, heavy look.
expertTake: The H.VERSAILTEX linen look blackout curtains are the top pick because they pair a natural texture with a coated back that blocks light. The LEMOMO black set is the value pick for plain, dark rooms. Skip lightweight blackout panels if you want true darkness, because light leaks around the edges unless the panels are wide and mounted close to the wall.
introParagraphs: Blackout curtains block daylight and glare, which helps with sleep, television and a room that faces a street lamp or a morning sun. Some also soften noise a little and reduce drafts near the glass.

The details that decide whether a set works are the lining or coating, the fullness of the panels, the header style and how close the rod sits to the wall. Even the best fabric leaks light if the panels are too narrow.

products.name: H.VERSAILTEX 100% Blackout Linen Look Curtains, 84 Inch, Natural
products.description:
H.VERSAILTEX sells a pair of faux linen panels, each 52 inches wide and 84 inches long, with a coated back for blackout performance. The linen look gives a casual texture that suits a living room better than a stark black panel. The listing says the materials passed a global recycled standard certificate.

The width of 52 inches per panel is generous, which helps with fullness and reduces light at the edges when the panels are hung on a rod with enough room. Compared with the LEMOMO, the H.VERSAILTEX is a softer, more decorative choice, but it costs more and wrinkles slightly more.

To maximize darkness, mount the rod 4 to 6 inches above the frame and extend it 3 to 6 inches past each side. Wash gently, and avoid high heat that can damage the coating. For a living room that needs both style and light control, it is the best balance here. If you own a steamer, hang the panels and steam them in place, because the folds drop out in minutes. A pair on a double rod with a sheer behind it also gives you a daytime option.
products.bestFor: Living rooms that want a linen texture and strong light control.
pros: 52 inch wide panels give good fullness

products.name: LEMOMO Black Blackout Curtains 52 x 84 Inch, Set of 2
products.description:
LEMOMO's black panels are 52 by 84 inches in 100 percent polyester, thermal insulated and room darkening. The listing says they impede 85 to 99 percent of light, which is honest about the fact that dark fabric without a coating is not a perfect blackout.

Black is the strongest color for light blocking, and polyester is easy to wash and wrinkle resistant. Compared with the H.VERSAILTEX, it is plainer and less expensive, and it does not have a textured look. In a dark bedroom it is the most direct solution.

Hang the panels on a sturdy rod and let them overlap at the center to prevent a light gap. Machine wash on a gentle cycle. It is an efficient, no frills blackout. Overlap the panels by a few inches at the center, and the 85 to 99 percent figure improves in practice.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and media rooms that need darkness at a lower tier.
cons: Light block is 85 to 99 percent, not a full 100

products.name: NICETOWN White 100% Blackout Curtains 84 Inch, Thermal, Noise Reducing
products.description:
NICETOWN's white panels measure 52 by 84 inches and use a sewn in blackout layer, with thermal insulation and some noise reduction. White blackout curtains keep a room bright by day and dark at night, which suits a living room with a lot of light.

A sewn in layer is more durable than a spray coating, though it makes the panel heavier. Compared with the LEMOMO, the NICETOWN offers a lighter, brighter look but at a slightly higher tier. Heavyweight panels can also dampen some sound, though not enough to count as soundproofing.

The weight needs a sturdy rod. Wash in a gentle cycle, and avoid hot dryers. It is a good choice for a bright living room. If you have a window with deep sill, hang the panels outside the frame so the lining clears it.
products.bestFor: Bright living rooms that want a white look and blackout at night.
pros: White keeps a room bright by day
cons: Heavy and needs a strong rod

products.name: ChrisDowa Light Gray 100% Blackout Curtains with Black Liner, 63 Inch

specList.label: Construction
specList.value: Two thick layers with black liner

products.description:
ChrisDowa makes a double layer panel with a black liner and a light gray face. The listing says it blocks all light and helps with noise. The 63 inch length suits a standard window above a sofa or a desk.

The black liner is the blocking layer, and the light gray face keeps the room's look from turning dark. Compared with the NICETOWN, it uses two thick layers, which makes it heavier. It also costs more.

Use a sturdy rod. Hang it so the hem clears the sill. It suits a gray or modern room. If you need more length, check the 84 inch version of the same style, because a 63 inch panel will stop well above the floor.
products.bestFor: Modern rooms that want light gray with a black liner.
cons: 63 inch length is short for some windows

products.name: Joydeco 100% Blackout Natural Linen Curtains 84 Inch, Rod Pocket and Back Tab

specList.label: Light block
specList.value: Described as 100 percent with UV block

products.description:
Joydeco offers a natural linen look panel with two hanging options, rod pocket and back tab. The 84 inch length suits standard ceilings, and the listing says it blocks light and UV.

The dual header gives flexibility. A rod pocket gathers the fabric into a casual fold, while back tabs create a cleaner pleat. Compared with the H.VERSAILTEX, it offers more hanging choices.

Rod pocket panels drag on the rod, so they do not slide as easily. Choose back tab for panels you open and close often. It is a flexible, stylish choice. If you are unsure which header to pick, hang a trial panel with back tabs first, because they are easy to change.
products.bestFor: Rooms where you want a choice of header styles.
cons: Rod pocket drags on the rod

products.name: SimpleHome Ombre Black to Gray White Blackout Curtains 52 x 84 Inch
products.description:
SimpleHome offers an ombre panel that fades from black to gray and white. The two tone gradient adds a decorative touch to a living room. Each panel is 52 by 84 inches.

The gradient adds style, and the listing says the fabric has no formaldehyde. Compared with the plain LEMOMO, it is more decorative.

An ombre design shows best when hung full. Overlap the panels and use a sturdy rod. It suits a modern room. Hang the dark end at the top and the pale end at the bottom to keep the gradient intentional.
products.bestFor: Modern rooms that want a gradient look.
cons: Not as dark as solid black

buyingCriteria.explanation: Blackout comes from a coating on the back, a sewn in liner or a triple weave. The H.VERSAILTEX uses a coated back, and the NICETOWN uses a sewn in layer. A bare dark polyester like the LEMOMO blocks 85 to 99 percent, not all. Check how the blackout is made. If you rent, a tension rod and a pair of clip rings give you a cheap, reversible way to try a blackout panel. A fast check is to hold the fabric against a bright window and see whether the light shows through; a coated or lined panel should look opaque.

Panels should be 1.5 to 2.5 times the window width. A 52 inch panel pair covers a window up to about 50 inches wide with good fullness. Narrow panels leave gaps that let light leak. A window 60 inches wide wants panels totaling at least 90 inches, so two 52 inch panels are about right. Panels hung flat look skimpy and leak light along the edges, so choose fullness over a lower tier if darkness matters.

Mount the rod 4 to 6 inches above the frame and 3 to 6 inches past each side. Light leaks over the top, so use a valance or a wrap around rod for total darkness. A rod too close to the glass lets light around the edges. If light still leaks above the rod, a simple cornice board or a valance can cover the gap. A pair of side return brackets that bend the rod toward the wall also close the side gaps, which is the cheapest way to stop light.

Grommet panels slide easily. Rod pockets, as on the Joydeco, gather but drag. Back tabs hide the rod. Pick based on how often you open them. Grommet panels are the easiest to open and close, and they suit rooms with daily use.

Panels should just touch the floor or hover about half an inch above it. The 84 inch panels suit standard 8 foot ceilings. A 63 inch panel, like the ChrisDowa, suits a window above a sofa. A hem that is slightly short looks tidy, while one that is too short looks like a mistake. Measure from the rod to the floor, then subtract about half an inch, and compare with the stated panel length.

Most polyester panels are machine washable on gentle. Avoid hot dryers that can crack the coating. Linen looks wrinkle, so steam them. Check the care label first, because a coated panel and a lined panel often need different washing. Hang the panels to air out for a day, because new coated fabric can carry a faint smell.

specDecoder.meaning: A blackout coating is an opaque layer applied to the back of the fabric. It blocks light but can crack if washed or dried too hot.
specDecoder.watchFor: The H.VERSAILTEX uses a coated back, so wash it gently and hang it to dry.

specDecoder.meaning: This number says how much light passes through the fabric. 100 percent is rarely achieved, because light also leaks around the edges.
specDecoder.watchFor: The LEMOMO lists 85 to 99 percent, which is honest for a dark, uncoated polyester.

specDecoder.meaning: A rod pocket is a sewn sleeve that the rod passes through. It gathers the fabric but does not glide easily.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Joydeco offers a rod pocket, so choose back tabs if you open the panels often.

specDecoder.meaning: Back tabs are loops sewn on the back of the panel. They hide the rod and give a clean fold.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Joydeco includes back tabs, which suit panels that stay mostly closed.

specDecoder.meaning: A thermal lining adds a layer that slows heat transfer through the window. It is a modest effect, not true insulation.
specDecoder.watchFor: The NICETOWN and LEMOMO list thermal insulation, so expect a small comfort gain near a cold window.

howWeEvaluated.title: Light control
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared coatings, liners and the stated light block. The H.VERSAILTEX's coated back and the NICETOWN's sewn in layer scored well, while the LEMOMO's honest 85 to 99 percent gave a realistic picture. Light control decides whether the curtain does its job.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fabric and look
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared linen looks, plain polyester and the ombre design. The H.VERSAILTEX and Joydeco give a textured living room look, while the LEMOMO is plain and dark. A curtain has to suit the room as well as darken it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and fullness
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared panel widths and lengths. The 52 inch panels on the H.VERSAILTEX, NICETOWN and LEMOMO give good fullness on a standard window. The ChrisDowa's 63 inch length suits a shorter window.

howWeEvaluated.title: Header and hanging
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rod pockets, back tabs and standard headers. The Joydeco's choice of two styles scored for flexibility. A header that glides makes daily use easier.

howWeEvaluated.title: Care and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered washing and wrinkles. Owner feedback patterns informed our advice to avoid hot dryers, which can crack a coating. Panels that wash easily earn more credit.

cards.label: Coated back
cards.text: The H.VERSAILTEX uses a coating on the back of a linen look fabric. It is lighter and drapes well, but the coating can crack if washed hot.

cards.label: Sewn in liner
cards.text: The NICETOWN and ChrisDowa use a separate layer. They are heavier, more durable and better at damping noise, but they need a sturdier rod.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Dark fabric or a black liner, wide panels that overlap in the center, and a rod mounted close to the wall. Add a valance or a wrap around rod to stop light at the top.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The LEMOMO black panels and the ChrisDowa black liner give the darkest rooms. The H.VERSAILTEX works if you want a lighter look with a coated back.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a textured fabric that looks like a decorative panel in a living room. The H.VERSAILTEX and Joydeco justify the higher tier.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The curtains are for a bedroom or a media room where you want darkness. The LEMOMO and SimpleHome cost less and do the job.

maintenance.why: Dust and skin oils build up on fabric. Use a gentle cycle and cool water, and hang or tumble dry on low.
Dust collects at the top and in the pleats. A brush attachment on low suction removes it.
Heavy blackout panels pull on the rod. Tighten brackets and add a center support if it bows.
Linen looks wrinkle easily, and a steamer restores the drape. Avoid high heat on the coating.
Cracks in a coating let light through. Replace panels that peel.

faq.q: Are blackout curtains really 100 percent dark?
faq.a: Rarely. The fabric may block nearly all light, but light still leaks around the edges and over the rod. For total darkness, use wide panels, mount the rod close to the wall and add a valance. A black liner behind a decorative front panel is the usual trick for a living room that needs both looks.

faq.q: How wide should blackout curtains be?
faq.a: Panels should be 1.5 to 2.5 times the window width, so that they hang in folds and overlap at the center. Flat, narrow panels let light leak. Measure the window and the rod length. If the window is wide, buy two pairs and hang four panels across the rod.

faq.q: Do blackout curtains insulate a room?
faq.a: They help a little by slowing heat transfer and blocking drafts near the glass. The effect is modest, not the same as true insulation. A lined panel works better than a thin one. A thick lined panel can also shade a window from afternoon sun, which helps a hot room.

faq.q: Can I machine wash blackout curtains?
faq.a: Most polyester panels can be washed on a gentle cycle in cool water. Hot dryers can crack a coating, so hang them or tumble on low. Check the label for your set.

faq.q: How high should I hang the rod?
faq.a: Mount the rod 4 to 6 inches above the window frame and 3 to 6 inches beyond each side. This makes the window look larger and reduces light leaks. Use a sturdy bracket for heavy panels.

Heavy, lined panels dampen some sound, though they are not soundproofing. They help with echo in a bare room. For real noise control, you need thicker materials. Layering heavy panels over a sheer adds a little more muffling.
